text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Austria will become part of the European Union's Schengen agreement by the end of the year, as Germany has withdrawn its threat to veto the country's membership. However the border to Austria's northernwestern neighbour will only be opened gradually until the end of 1998.
- Austria's tourism industry fears another setback this summer. Economic researchers downgrade their forecasts.

- Adding his voice to a growing row between the ruling coalition partners, parliamentary President and Social Democrat vice-leader Heinz Fischer says Austria will certainly not join NATO in 1999. Fischer accuses Defence Minister Werner Fasslabend of being too unrealistic on the issue. However, he said his party is willing to talk about joining a reformed NATO.

- Austria's postal monopoly Post & Telekom Austria's privatisation is threatened by the conservative People's Party demand that the postal employees social plan on early retirement must also be adapted for teachers.
- Building societies harshly criticise the government's plan to stop public funding of their premiums.
- Austria's national lottery company Oesterreichische Lotterien has felt the effects of the government's austerity measures as turnover fell 4.4. percent to 14.5 billion schillings.
- Germany's electricity giant Bayernwerke is said to be standing behind Styria's regional energy provider Steweag's bid for a 25 percent stake in Upper Austria's OKA.

- Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, state secretary in the Finance Ministry, believes Austria's deficit will be below 3.0 percent this year. He also expects Austria to meet the Maastricht crteria in 1998 and 1999 too.
DIE PRESSE
- Experts are negotiating plans to raise the legal age of retirement from 65 years to 66.
- The coalition parties' pensioners groups demand public pensions must be raised by at least the rate of inflation in 1998 and 1999.
- A lawyer has taken legal action against Bank Austria saying one of the bank's share issuing prospectuses was missing information and therefore the bank contravened Austria's shareholder law.
- The decision on who will take over the stake in Upper Austria's regional energy provider OKA could be a key to Austria's future strucure electricity industry.

- Unemployment is a threat to the introduction of the euro. However, both vice-Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel as well as central bank President Klaus Liebscher say it will either be introduced now or never.
KURIER
- Raiffeisen head Walter Rothensteiner wants better confidentiality in banking.
- Luxembourg's future European Council President Jacques Poos said in Vienna his country does not favour the harmonisation of taxes as demanded by Austria and Germany.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Retailer Rewe will open 100 new shops of its chemist's chain Bipa in order to secure its leading position in Austria.
- Bank Austria and Creditanstalt's eastern European business will merge under a joint holding. Germany's WestLB and Italy's Cariplo might participate in this holding with their own subsidiaries.
